    - tabpanel "Lesson interaction and visualization":
      - region "Simple English explanation of Truth Tables":
        - group:
          - text: In simple English
          - heading "Understand Truth Tables" [level=2]
      - text: DISCRETE AND APPLIED MATHEMATICS COMBINATORICS, GRAPH THEORY AND LOGIC
      - heading "587 Truth Tables" [level=1]
      - paragraph: Evaluate logical expressions using truth tables.
      - text: "Level: Intermediate-Advanced Topic: Discrete Math Lab Tools: Spreadsheet + Scripting Time: 6-10 min"
      - navigation:
        - button "Interact"
        - button "Learn"
        - button "Worked Example"
        - button "Formula"
        - button "Practice"
      - complementary:
        - heading "1 Observe" [level=2]
        - paragraph: Truth values for the basic statements.
        - text: p A statement
        - button "Toggle p truth value": T
        - text: q Another statement
        - button "Toggle q truth value": F
        - article:
          - img
          - text: Tip
          - paragraph: Toggle p and q to highlight their matching row instantly.
      - main:
        - heading "2 Manipulate" [level=2]
        - paragraph: Choose a compound statement and watch the truth table fill.
        - text: Choose a statement
        - combobox "Truth table statement":
          - option "p → q" [selected]
          - option "p ∧ q"
          - option "p ∨ q"
          - option "p ↔ q"
        - text: Proposition (read in words)
        - status "Proposition (read in words)": If p, then q
        - table:
          - rowgroup:
            - row "p q p → q":
              - columnheader "p"
              - columnheader "q"
              - columnheader "p → q"
          - rowgroup:
            - row "T T T":
              - cell "T"
              - cell "T"
              - cell "T"
            - row "T F F":
              - cell "T"
              - cell "F"
              - cell "F"
            - row "F T T":
              - cell "F"
              - cell "T"
              - cell "T"
            - row "F F T":
              - cell "F"
              - cell "F"
              - cell "T"
        - complementary:
          - heading "Result" [level=2]
          - strong:
            - img
            - text: Contingent
          - paragraph: It is a contingent statement.
          - separator
          - paragraph: T True
          - paragraph: F False
        - img
        - text: p → q is false only when p is true and q is false.
      - article:
        - heading "3 Notice the pattern" [level=2]
        - paragraph: Key observation from the table.
        - complementary:
          - img
          - text: Observation
          - paragraph: The statement is false in the rows determined by its connective.
          - paragraph: So, p → q is contingent.
      - article:
        - heading "4 Understand the rule" [level=2]
        - paragraph: Key rule / definition.
        - complementary:
          - text: Key Rule (p → q)
          - strong: false only when p is true and q is false.
          - paragraph: Classification
          - list:
            - listitem: Always True → Tautology
            - listitem: Always False → Contradiction
            - listitem: Otherwise → Contingent
      - article:
        - heading "5 Watch out!" [level=2]
        - paragraph: Common misconception.
        - complementary:
          - img
          - text: Common Mistake
          - paragraph: Thinking p → q is the same as q → p.
          - paragraph: "Let p=T, q=F: p→q is F, but q→p is T."
      - heading "Worked Example" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Evaluate the statement p ∧ q using a truth table and classify it.
      - table:
        - rowgroup:
          - row "p q p ∧ q":
            - columnheader "p"
            - columnheader "q"
            - columnheader "p ∧ q"
        - rowgroup:
          - row "T T T":
            - cell "T"
            - cell "T"
            - cell "T"
          - row "T F F":
            - cell "T"
            - cell "F"
            - cell "F"
          - row "F T F":
            - cell "F"
            - cell "T"
            - cell "F"
          - row "F F F":
            - cell "F"
            - cell "F"
            - cell "F"
      - complementary:
        - heading "Conclusion" [level=2]
        - paragraph: p ∧ q is True only when both p and q are True.
        - paragraph: Therefore, p ∧ q is contingent.
      - heading "Try Independently" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Your turn! Build the table and classify the statement.
      - article:

        - paragraph: Construct the truth table for p ∨ q and classify it.
